system:
You are a senior methodologist designing candidate analysis plans for a biomedical data-analysis agent. You receive a compiled objective, a measured data profile with numbered difficulties, a catalogue of executable components, lessons from earlier projects, and resource limits. Design 1 complete, executable, genuinely different analysis plans.

The candidate pool is built over several calls so that each plan can be thought through properly. This is call 6 of 8 in this round; 5 plan(s) proposed earlier are listed at the end of the user message. Your plans must differ in design from all of them and widen the coverage of the three diversity directions.

What a plan is
A plan is a whole analysis design, not a model name: analysis unit, inputs and their representation, preprocessing, model, training, the plan's own validation design, metrics, and the conclusion it would be entitled to draw. Each plan will be executed exactly as you write it, so every field must be concrete.

Level of ambition
- Design at the level a methods paper would use, not at the level of a textbook exercise. This question is hard because many approaches are feasible and the complex ones can fail in ways a score does not show.
- A simple reference plan has already been proposed. Every plan in this call must be ambitious.
- Ambitious plans (complexity "ambitious") are deep, non-linear, joint latent-variable, gene- or patient-specific multi-component designs, or combinations of these, built mainly from the AMBITIOUS tier. Ridge, k-nearest-neighbour and partial-least-squares regressions are baselines and may not be the core of an ambitious plan.
- Complexity earns nothing by itself. Each ambitious plan must say which measured difficulty it addresses and why the added machinery should help with it.

Diversity
Spread the plans along three directions and use at least two clearly different values on each:
- data: which inputs and representations;
- model: model type and capacity;
- method: overall strategy (for example per-feature versus joint modelling, single model versus ensemble, how modalities are fused, how the validation is designed).
Do not submit two plans that differ only by a hyper-parameter or an encoder name.

Validity
- Respect allowed and forbidden inputs of the objective.
- Each plan chooses its own validation design from the options in the catalogue and reports its own score with it. Choose it deliberately; it will be judged.
- Every ambitious plan must be able to show a training curve and a convergence statement, and a direct comparison with the simple reference and the required comparators.
- Declare a budget. A full run of one plan must fit in 120 minutes on one job (16 CPU cores; a GPU may or may not be available, so say whether the plan needs one).

Components
Use component keys and parameter names exactly as in the catalogue. If an idea needs a component the catalogue lacks, you may propose it: put a new key in model.component and describe it in new_components (name, what it computes, inputs, outputs, training). Proposals are implemented only if feasible within the budget, so at most 1 plans may depend on a new component.

Be compact: summary at most 90 words, rationale at most 50 words, no padding in any field.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"plans": [ {
  "plan_id": any short label,
  "name": short name,
  "summary": 3-5 sentences in plain language describing the design and what it would let us conclude; no results, no predictions of scores,
  "complexity": "simple_reference" | "ambitious",
  "analysis_unit": string,
  "inputs": object following the catalogue's input representations,
  "preprocessing": [string],
  "model": {"component": key, "params": {...}},
  "fusion": string or null (only where the catalogue defines fusion),
  "training": {...},
  "validation": {...},
  "metrics": [string],
  "allowed_conclusions": string,
  "budget": {"needs_gpu": bool, "pilot_minutes": number, "full_minutes": number, "cpus": integer},
  "diversity": {"data": short label, "model": short label, "method": short label},
  "rationale": 2-4 sentences,
  "difficulties_addressed": [difficulty ids],
  "new_components": [ {"name": key, "description": string} ]
} ] }
prompt:
COMPILED OBJECTIVE:
{
 "question": "From the H&E pathology images alone, how much of the PAM50 subtype information can be predicted?",
 "task_family": "single_modality_classification",
 "analysis_unit": "patient",
 "estimand": "Patient-level out-of-fold macro-F1 and paired gain over chance (plus proportion of class-prior deviance explained) for predicting four-class PAM50 subtype from H&E image features alone.",
 "target": "Four-class PAM50 intrinsic breast cancer subtype (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) per labelled patient.",
 "allowed_inputs": [
  "Patient-mean H&E foundation-model feature vectors (UNI2-h, CONCH-Z, Virchow2, MUSK, H-Optimus-1)",
  "Tile-level H&E foundation-model feature vectors (up to 128 tiles per slide across the five encoders)",
  "Patient and slide identifiers for patient-level aggregation and split grouping",
  "Collection site identifier solely for defining site-held-out cross-validation splits (never as a predictor)",
  "Unlabelled patients' H&E image features solely for fold-internal unsupervised representation fitting if used (never scored)"
 ],
 "forbidden_inputs": [
  "er, pr, her2 (immunohistochemistry receptor statuses)",
  "histological_type",
  "age and stage",
  "RNA expression or RNA-derived variables",
  "site (as a model input feature)"
 ],
 "forbidden_reasons": {
  "er, pr, her2 (immunohistochemistry receptor statuses)": "Receptor statuses are separate clinical measurements correlated with PAM50; including them creates a non-image clinical shortcut and invalidates H&E-only predictability.",
  "histological_type": "Recorded histological type is a curated clinical-pathological variable rather than raw H&E image features, violating the restriction to H&E images alone.",
  "age and stage": "Patient age and tumour stage are non-image clinical variables; using them estimates multimodal prediction rather than information present in H&E images alone.",
  "RNA expression or RNA-derived variables": "PAM50 subtypes are defined directly from tumour RNA expression, so any RNA-derived feature leaks the target construction and invalidates image-based prediction.",
  "site (as a model input feature)": "Collection site is non-image institutional metadata associated with PAM50 class (Cramer's V = 0.21); using it as a predictor exploits technical confounding."
 },
 "required_comparators": [
  "Majority-class null classifier fit on training folds (guards against majority-subtype collapse under class imbalance)",
  "Stratified class-prior null baseline fit on training folds (zero-information ruler for macro-F1, AUROC, and log-loss entropy)",
  "Simple image-only reference: class-weighted regularised multinomial logistic regression on single-encoder patient-mean H&E features"
 ],
 "primary_metric": "Out-of-fold four-class macro-F1 (and paired macro-F1 difference above chance floors) across repeated nested patient-level cross-validation with 95% patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals",
 "secondary_metrics": [
  "Proportion of class-prior multi-class log-loss (Shannon entropy) explained out-of-fold with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI",
  "Macro and per-class one-vs-rest AUROC with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs",
  "Per-class recall, precision, and F1 across LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2 (highlighting minority Her2 and LumA-versus-LumB separation)",
  "Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference versus the simple patient-mean logistic regression reference with 95% bootstrap CI",
  "Site-held-out grouped cross-validation macro-F1 and paired gain over chance (19 collection sites) with 95% bootstrap CI"
 ],
 "acceptance_criteria": [
  {
   "id": "A1",
   "statement": "Predictors use only H&E image features; clinical, immunohistochemistry receptor, RNA-derived, and site variables are excluded from model inputs.",
   "check": "no_forbidden_inputs",
   "rule": "Pass requires zero forbidden variables in any model input or preprocessing step; site is permitted only to define held-out validation splits."
  },
  {
   "id": "A2",
   "statement": "All slides and tiles of each patient stay on the same side of every split and bootstrap resample.",
   "check": "correct_split_unit",
   "rule": "Group all slide and tile records by patient ID so train and evaluation patient sets have zero overlap in every fold."
  },
  {
   "id": "A3",
   "statement": "Encoder choice, tile-versus-mean level, dimensionality reduction, class weights, and hyperparameters are selected strictly within inner training folds.",
   "check": "selection_nested",
   "rule": "Select the configuration maximising inner-fold macro-F1 without accessing outer-fold patient features or labels across repeated nested cross-validation."
  },
  {
   "id": "A4",
   "statement": "Out-of-fold H&E macro-F1 exceeds data-derived majority-class and training-prior chance baselines on the labelled cohort.",
   "check": "beats_required_floors",
   "rule": "Floor thresholds are derived directly as out-of-fold macro-F1 of majority-class and stratified class-prior predictors fit on identical training folds."
  },
  {
   "id": "A5",
   "statement": "Any complex tile-level or multi-encoder method is benchmarked directly against simple patient-mean class-weighted regularised logistic regression.",
   "check": "beats_simple_reference",
   "rule": "Reference score is out-of-fold macro-F1 of inner-tuned regularised multinomial logistic regression on patient-mean H&E features on identical splits."
  },
  {
   "id": "A6",
   "statement": "Iterative or neural H&E classifiers demonstrate stabilised training loss or inner validation metric before termination.",
   "check": "training_converged",
   "rule": "Convergence is verified when solver tolerance is met or trailing-epoch loss slope stops improving relative to earlier training epochs inside folds."
  },
  {
   "id": "A7",
   "statement": "All compared H&E models and null baselines are scored on the exact same labelled patients and fold assignments.",
   "check": "both_arms_same_units",
   "rule": "Require identical labelled patient IDs, identical outer fold indices, and identical exclusion of unlabelled patients from scoring across all arms."
  },
  {
   "id": "A8",
   "statement": "Primary macro-F1 and paired differences against comparators are reported with 95% patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals.",
   "check": "interval_reported",
   "rule": "Resample labelled patients with replacement across aggregated repeated outer-fold predictions to derive percentile 95% confidence bounds."
  }
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "Broad predictability: H&E macro-F1 beats chance (95% CI) in both patient and site-held-out CV, with all four classes beating chance; report macro-F1 and entropy-explained 95% intervals.",
  "Partial predictability: H&E macro-F1 beats chance (95% CI) in both patient and site-held-out CV, but at least one PAM50 class fails to beat chance at 95% confidence.",
  "Site-confounded predictability: H&E macro-F1 beats chance (95% CI) in patient-level CV, but its paired 95% interval over chance in site-held-out CV includes or falls below zero.",
  "Insufficient evidence of predictability: the paired 95% confidence interval for H&E-only macro-F1 over the chance floor in patient-level nested CV includes or falls below zero."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Applies to standalone H&E subtype prediction in TCGA-BRCA patients using these five frozen encoders; does not establish incremental gain over clinical variables, biological mechanism, or external clinical utility.",
 "notes": "Per D5, clinical and receptor variables are forbidden because the question asks what H&E alone predicts, overriding the incremental-value template; use fold-internal class weighting inside repeated nested patient CV."
}

DATASET DESCRIPTION (from the data provider):
name: TCGA-BRCA diagnostic slides with clinical variables
unit: patient
description: 'Breast cancer patients with H&E whole-slide images and six clinical variables: age, stage, histological
  type, and the receptor statuses ER, PR and HER2 from immunohistochemistry. Images are represented by frozen pathology
  foundation models: five encoders, each giving one feature vector per tile (up to 128 tiles per slide, identical
  tile positions across encoders) and a mean-pooled vector per patient. The label is the PAM50 intrinsic subtype
  in four classes. Patients without a label still have images. Each patient has a collection site.'
label_provenance:
  statement: PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is
    a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50
    for a substantial share of tumours).
  implication: 'No RNA-derived variable may be used as an input. Whether receptors may be used depends on the question
    asked: they are a legitimate baseline when the question is what images add to clinical information, and a forbidden
    shortcut when the question is what images alone contain.'
scope_of_inference: incremental predictive value in this cohort; not an independent biological mechanism
how_predictions_are_scored: The evaluator re-runs every method inside its own repeated nested cross-validation on
  the labelled patients (outer 5 folds repeated 3 times, patient-level; any model or configuration choice happens
  only inside the training folds) and compares it with a fixed, fully tuned clinical-only model on the same patients
  and folds.
rulers:
  floor_clinical: clinical variables only, fixed and fully tuned by the evaluator; the gain is measured against
    it
  simple_reference: clinical variables plus mean-pooled image features in a logistic regression; complex methods
    are compared with it
  historical_reference: an earlier project's late fusion reached macro-F1 0.723 on a single 121-patient test split
    (not ground truth)
decision_rule: 'Primary metric: paired difference in macro-F1 (image plus clinical minus clinical only) with a patient-level
  bootstrap 95% interval. Conclusion, from the interval alone: "improves" if the lower bound is above 0; "insufficient
  evidence" if the interval contains 0; "worse" if the upper bound is below 0. Secondary: log-loss difference, one-vs-rest
  AUROC difference, per-class recall changes (LumA and LumB in particular), and a site-held-out sensitivity analysis.
  Both arms must use the same patients and the same missing-value handling.'
deliverable: The estimated gain with its interval, the three-way conclusion, out-of-fold predictions for both arms,
  and the per-class changes.

MEASURED DATA PROFILE:

 "n_units_with_images": 1061,
 "n_labelled": 802,
 "n_unlabelled": 259,
 "classes": [
  "LumA",
  "LumB",
  "Basal",
  "Her2"
 ],
 "n_slides": 1132,
 "n_tiles": 135911,
 "modalities": {
  "clinical": {
   "variables": [
    "age",
    "stage",
    "histological_type",
    "er",
    "pr",
    "her2"
   ]
  },
  "image": {
   "encoders": {
    "UNI2-h": 1536,
    "CONCH-Z": 768,
    "Virchow2": 2560,
    "MUSK": 1024,
    "H-Optimus-1": 1536
   },
   "levels": [
    "tile (up to 128 per slide)",
    "patient mean"
   ]
  }
 },
 "grouping": {
  "column": "site",
  "n_groups": 19
 }
}

MEASURED DIFFICULTIES (most severe first):
- D1 [class_imbalance, severity high] Class counts among 802 labelled patients: LumA 410, LumB 190, Basal 137, Her2 65. The smallest class is 8.1% of the cohort. Implication: Use a class-balanced metric and class weighting; an unweighted model can score well while missing the smallest class entirely.
- D2 [missingness, severity high] Share of labelled patients without a definite value: er 4.7% (missing 4.5%), pr 5.1% (missing 4.6%), her2 31.8% (missing 15.3%), stage 2.6% (missing 2.6%), histological_type 0.1% (missing 0.1%), age 0.0% (missing 0.0%). Implication: Handle missing values inside each training fold with an explicit missing level, identically in both comparison arms.
- D3 [small_n_large_p, severity high] 802 labelled patients against image features of 1536 (UNI2-h), 768 (CONCH-Z), 2560 (Virchow2), 1024 (MUSK), 1536 (H-Optimus-1) dimensions per encoder. Implication: High-capacity image models overfit easily; regularise, reduce dimension inside folds, and require evidence of convergence and of a gain over a simple reference.
- D4 [technical_confounding, severity high] Labelled patients come from 19 collection sites (largest 130 patients, 3 sites with fewer than 10). Image features (UNI2-h) identify the site of a patient with accuracy 0.89 against 0.17 for always guessing the largest site; site and class are associated (Cramer's V = 0.21). Implication: Part of an image-based gain may come from site signatures; a site-held-out sensitivity analysis should accompany the main estimate.
- D5 [label_provenance, severity high] PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50 for a substantial share of tumours). Implication: No RNA-derived variable may be used as an input. Whether receptors may be used depends on the question asked: they are a legitimate baseline when the question is what images add to clinical information, and a forbidden shortcut when the question is what images alone contain.
- D6 [hierarchy, severity medium] 46 labelled patients have more than one slide; tiles per patient range from 6 to 471 (median 124). Implication: The patient is the unit of analysis: all slides and tiles of a patient must stay on the same side of every split.
- D7 [strong_baseline, severity medium] Clinical variables alone reach macro-F1 0.576 in 5-fold cross-validation; recall by class: LumA 0.54, LumB 0.54, Basal 0.82, Her2 0.52. The weakest class is Her2. Implication: The question is about what images add to this baseline, so the clinical arm must be tuned as carefully as the image arm and evaluated on the same patients.
- D8 [statistical_power, severity medium] For a simple image-plus-clinical model against clinical only, the paired macro-F1 difference has a bootstrap standard error of 0.021 with one 5-fold split of 802 patients. The smallest difference detectable with 80% power is about 0.059. Implication: Gains of a few points cannot be established from one split; use repeated cross-validation and report an interval, not only a point estimate.
- D9 [multiple_comparisons, severity medium] 5 image encoders are available, each usable at tile or patient level with several fusion strategies. Implication: Choosing the best of many configurations on the evaluation folds inflates the reported gain; selection must be nested or counted.

COMPONENT CATALOGUE:
TASK FAMILY: single_modality_classification - Estimate how well one modality alone predicts a class label.

INPUT REPRESENTATIONS (field inputs):
  - image: Frozen foundation-model features. Tile level keeps up to 128 tiles per slide (all slides of a patient pooled into one bag); patient level is the mean over tiles. Parameters: encoders [subset of the available encoders]; level tile | patient; reduce {type pca | linear_projection | none, dim}.
  - clinical: Clinical covariates, one-hot encoded with an explicit missing level inside each training fold. Parameters: variables [age, stage, histological_type, er, pr, her2]; use true | false.

BASIC TIER (baselines, the single simple reference, preprocessing):
  - clinical_only: Clinical variables only (logistic regression / boosting). The comparison arm. Parameters: tune true | false. Cost: seconds.
  - patient_mean_logreg: Clinical variables concatenated with PCA-reduced mean-pooled image features, multinomial logistic regression. The simple reference. Parameters: grid over encoder, n_pca, C. Cost: seconds per fit.

AMBITIOUS TIER (what candidate plans are mainly built from):
  - attention_mil: Multiple-instance learning over tiles: a learned attention or transformer aggregator turns a patient's tiles into one embedding. Parameters: aggregator gated_attention | multihead_attention | transformer; heads; layers; embed_dim; dropout. Cost: 1-3 minutes per fit on 16 CPUs.
  - multi_encoder_fusion: Fuse several foundation models: attention or gating over encoders, per tile (tiles are aligned across encoders) or per patient. Parameters: level tile | patient; encoder_fusion attention | gated | concat; aggregator (tile level); embed_dim. Cost: 2-6 minutes per fit on 16 CPUs.
  - morphology_prototypes: Cluster training tiles into morphological prototypes; describe each patient by the share of tiles per prototype (plus clinical variables). Parameters: n_prototypes 8-64; encoder; classifier logreg | gbm. Cost: under a minute per fit.
  - conditional_fusion: Let clinical variables condition the image branch: feature-wise modulation of tile embeddings (FiLM) or clinical-query cross-attention over tiles. Parameters: mode film | cross_attention; aggregator; embed_dim. Cost: 1-3 minutes per fit on 16 CPUs.
  - incremental_offset: Fit the clinical model first, freeze its class logits as an offset, and train the image branch only on what the clinical model leaves unexplained. Aims directly at incremental value. Parameters: image_branch {level, aggregator, embed_dim}; init_zero true | false. Cost: 1-3 minutes per fit on 16 CPUs.
  - hierarchical: Two-stage classifier: separate the coarse groups first, then a dedicated image-driven model for the pair clinical variables separate worst. Parameters: groups [[LumA, LumB], [Basal], [Her2]]; fine_inputs image | image+clinical; image_branch {..}. Cost: 2-4 minutes per fit on 16 CPUs.
  - ssl_preadapted_mil: Self-supervised pre-adaptation of the tile aggregator (two random tile subsets of one patient should agree) on training-fold and unlabelled patients, then supervised training. Pre-adaptation is redone inside every training fold. Parameters: pretrain_epochs; uses_unlabelled true | false; then the attention_mil params. Cost: 3-8 minutes per fit on 16 CPUs.
  - gradient_boosting: Gradient-boosted trees on clinical variables plus PCA-reduced patient-level image features. Parameters: n_pca; max_iter; learning_rate. Cost: seconds per fit.
  - stacking_ensemble: Stack heterogeneous models through out-of-fold class probabilities with a logistic meta-learner fitted inside the training fold. Parameters: members [list of {component, params, inputs, fusion}]; meta logreg. Cost: (inner folds + 1) x the summed cost of the members.

FUSION: How clinical information joins the image branch (field 'fusion'): early_concat | late_average | offset | film | cross_attention | none. Any neural component may set, in model.params: aggregator, encoder_fusion, embed_dim, dropout, head flat | hierarchical.

TRAINING OPTIONS (field training): max_epochs; early_stopping_patience; lr; weight_decay; class_weighting balanced | none; augmentation {tile_resample: tiles drawn per bag per epoch, mixup_alpha, tile_dropout}; n_seeds_ensemble 1-3; tuning.grid: up to 4 alternative settings of model/training parameters the plan wants selected

VALIDATION DESIGN OPTIONS (field validation): scheme kfold | repeated_kfold; k 3-5; repeats 1-3; split_unit patient | slide | tile; selection nested (configuration chosen inside each training fold) | same_folds (configuration chosen on the folds that are also reported) | none; inner_k 2-3; clinical_comparator {tuned true | false}; interval bootstrap

LESSONS FROM EARLIER PROJECTS (retrieved by difficulty):
- K6 (Project 3): Fusion that included ER/PR/HER2 scored macro-F1 0.723, image only 0.645, and fusion without receptors 0.583. Which number answers the question depends on whether receptors are part of the question. Practice: Decide allowed and forbidden inputs from the question, and compare the arms the question names.
- K5 (Project 3): The objective required the joint representation to preserve structure at least as well as the best single modality; the selected model had a clustering ARI of 0.528 against 0.613 for RNA alone, and nobody checked. Practice: Turn every requirement in the objective into an explicit check that runs before a result is reported.
- K9 (Project 3): Patients with several slides and site-specific staining make random tile- or slide-level splits optimistic. Practice: Split by patient; add a site-held-out analysis when sites differ in class mix.
- K1 (Project 1, first version): Two runs with identical inputs selected different methods because the deciding margin was smaller than run-to-run variation (a sub-second runtime difference broke the tie). Practice: Before ranking, measure the spread of the selection signal across seeds or resamples; treat differences inside that spread as ties.
- K8 (Project 3): A baseline labelled as an ATAC decoder actually returned RNA principal components, and a re-implemented method overlapped the reference implementation at only 0.195. Practice: Check each baseline does what its name says on a case with a known answer before using it as a comparator.
- K10 (Projects 1-3): Planning was a rule-based filter over methods; alternatives were never compared as whole analysis designs, and the reports listed numbers without a conclusion. Practice: Compare complete plans (inputs, model, validation, permitted conclusion) and end with a stated conclusion and its limits.
- K3 (Project 2, first version): Four generative models were trained for about one minute in total; their samples were noise, and the negative conclusion followed from the tiny budget, not from the data. Practice: A complex model needs a training curve and a convergence statement before its score is read; an unconverged model is evidence about the budget only.
- K7 (Project 3): A fusion head trained with unweighted cross-entropy recalled 0 of 10 patients of the smallest class while its macro score still looked acceptable. Practice: Weight classes, use a class-balanced metric, and report recall for every class.
